intended_object: The covariance matrix of a measure μ on ℝ^ι (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι): the matrix whose (i, j) entry is Cov_μ(z_i, z_j), the covariance of the i-th and j-th coordinates. This comes from the docstring.
explanation:
The body is `fun i j => cov[fun z => z i, fun z => z i; μ]`. Both arguments are the i-th coordinate, and the index j is never used. So entry (i, j) is Var_μ(z_i), not Cov_μ(z_i, z_j), which contradicts the docstring.

Counterexample: let ι = Fin 2 and let μ be the law of (X, −X) with X a standard Gaussian. The true covariance matrix is [[1, −1], [−1, 1]]. This definition gives [[1, 1], [1, 1]], because every entry in row i equals Var(z_i). More generally, the definition returns a matrix with constant rows, which is not symmetric unless all variances are equal. The fix is to put `fun z => z j` in the second argument.

Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.covarianceBilin` (the covariance bilinear form, defined in general Hilbert spaces) encodes the correct object. Evaluated on the basis vectors, it gives the intended matrix entries.
